bullets: Sustainability is a systems-thinking problem before it's an environmental problem — ignoring that leads to repeated, unnecessary work.
The most expensive thing about climate change is the optionality lost by delaying action — early decisions shape long-term outcomes.
Carbon accounting requires the rigor of double-entry bookkeeping to be effective — this structural integrity is often overlooked.
Risk management at planetary scale resembles reliability engineering at company scale — both demand disciplined tradeoff analysis.
Project Drawdown illustrates how systems thinking reveals clean, scalable solutions — the second-order effects are most often missed.
Teams using Carbon Trust demonstrate that trade-offs become visible when systems are mapped — framing determines which choices are prioritized.
Reliability engineering at organizational scale mirrors planetary risk management — both depend on consistent, repeatable processes.
Running a concept for two weeks enables iteration — the real test is in execution, not just idea generation.
